content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against its evidence. The root-cause claim is presented as fact, but it rests on an unrun reading of the source, so I'm treating it as unverified. The plain-words version says a flag came on and that the affected pages returned errors, which the evidence supports, though "likely fails" is hedged.

I'm rechecking the causal-chain claim, since "kept climbing until highest at 04:19" implies a steady rise that the record doesn't actually show. The only per-minute detail I have is the flag share going partial at 04:13 and full at 04:14, so I'm treating the steady-climb wording as unsupported.

I'm checking the causal-chain claim that the error rate "kept climbing until highest at 04:19," since the only per-minute information I have doesn't show a steady rise. The stated range of 0.5% to 40.5%, with a peak at the final minute, is consistent with a rise, but the record gives no series to confirm it, so I'm flagging that wording as unsupported. The ZeroDivisionError first appearing at 04:13 checks out, since the logs I read start at 03:43 and show nothing before that. The flag history is also consistent: off for every evaluation through 04:12, partial at 04:13, and fully on from 04:14, with no changes showing in the flag provider's record.

I'm checking whether the ruled-out claim about client disconnects stands: the disconnect logs stop at the onset minute, and the error rate held at its usual 1.00% before then, so that holds. Next I'm looking at the closing claim that cites F1, which I'll check against whether the source is named.

I'm checking the CF1 and CF2 claims against the record: the flag went from partial at 04:13 to fully on at 04:14, and no rollout stage or check appears in the logs to have held or reversed it. The CF3 claim, that the flag change never showed in the provider history or production, still needs checking against the change records.

I'm going through the remaining claims about the flag change and the earlier check, confirming that the record shows no rollout stage holding or reversing the flag and no change in the provider history or production events. The what-if about Argus leaving the undo to a person is consistent with the record too, so I'll keep it in mind while I look at the action items.

content.text:
I found one claim the record doesn't support. In causal_chain 1, the document says the account page error rate "kept climbing" until its peak. The record gives no minute-by-minute figures. It gives only the 1% baseline, the 30.8% average while broken, the range in Gbac1 and the 04:19 peak. The only "rose step by step" wording comes from Code-Fix's own reading in F1, and nothing confirms it.

The record supports every other claim. Where a claim rests on Code-Fix's reading, the document either says it is unverified or cites F1 as its source. I didn't judge the action items or the what-if halves of the contributing factors.

flags.quote: the account page error rate kept climbing until it was highest at {Gbac1.7}
flags.why: The record shows only a range of 0.50%–40.50% with a peak at 04:19 and a 30.8% average while broken; there are no per-minute figures showing a continuous climb, and 'step by step' comes only from Code-Fix's unverified reading.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary runs average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases they made this month without handling a shopper who bought nothing this month, so for any shopper who has bought before but not this month the page raises ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

A setting that shows shoppers their spending this month came on, and the code behind it likely fails when a shopper has bought nothing yet this month, so those shoppers' account pages returned errors.

Account pages of shoppers who have not bought anything this month could keep failing while the monthly spend feature stays on, and the feature could come on again without any change showing in the flag provider's history.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 during {G5309.3}. This error did not appear in the log lines before the onset.

The monthly-spend-feature flag was off for every evaluation during {G7e5d.4}. It was on for part of the evaluations at {G971b.6} (on {G971b.2}, off {G971b.1} of {G971b.3}) and on for every evaluation during {Gce95.4}.
Neither the production change events read at {T9.1} nor the flag provider's history read at {T15.1} shows this change, so the record does not show what switched the flag.
All replicas ran the same revision when read at {T10.1}, but the record does not show whether that revision was already running before the onset, so a change to it was not ruled out.
The client-disconnect failures on account pages: they were logged well before the onset while the account page error rate stayed at its usual {Gbac1.6}, and they stopped at the onset.

With the flag on, the account page runs average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month and fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
No check was seen that ran the spend summary with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on for shoppers.
The flag went from on for part of the evaluations to on for all of them by the next minute. No rollout stage was seen that held or reversed it as account page errors rose.
The flag coming on did not appear in the flag provider's history or in the production change events, so the change was not in the record of what changed.
No on-call incident was linked to the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop, so nobody was paged.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one
